tools/absd.html.quickAnswer: Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty is the surcharge on top of BSD when you buy residential property. Singapore Citizens pay 0% on the first home, 20% on the second and 30% on the third or more; PRs pay 5% then 30% then 35%; foreigners pay 60%; entities 65%.

faqs.q: How much ABSD do I pay on a second property as a Singapore Citizen?
faqs.a: A Singapore Citizen pays 20% ABSD on a second residential property, charged on the higher of the purchase price or market value. On a S$1.5M purchase that is S$300,000 in ABSD, separate from and on top of the Buyer's Stamp Duty. This calculator returns both figures and the combined total for your exact price.

faqs.q: Can I use my CPF to pay ABSD?
faqs.a: No. ABSD must be paid in cash and is due within 14 days of signing the Option to Purchase or the Sale and Purchase Agreement. Unlike BSD, which CPF can cover on residential property, ABSD has no CPF route, so plan that working capital before you sign anything.

faqs.q: What ABSD rate applies when a Citizen buys jointly with a foreigner?
faqs.a: When buyers have different profiles, IRAS applies the highest applicable rate to the entire purchase price. So a Singapore Citizen buying jointly with a foreigner is assessed at the foreigner rate of 60% on the whole property, not a blend. Getting the ownership structure right before committing is where the real planning happens.

faqs.q: Do my overseas properties count toward my ABSD property count?
faqs.a: Yes. Your property count includes all residential properties you hold at the time of purchase, locally and overseas. If you already own a home abroad, your Singapore purchase may be treated as a second property and taxed accordingly. Declare honestly, because IRAS can reassess and claw back unpaid ABSD with penalties.

faqs.q: Can married couples avoid ABSD on their first home?
faqs.a: A married couple where at least one spouse is a Singapore Citizen, buying their first residential property jointly as their matrimonial home, may apply for ABSD remission. Couples where one is a Citizen and one a PR upgrading may also qualify. Your conveyancer confirms eligibility, since the conditions are specific and easy to fail.

tools/bsd.html.quickAnswer: Buyer's Stamp Duty is the base stamp duty every Singapore property buyer pays regardless of citizenship or how many homes they own. Residential BSD is tiered: 1% on the first S$180k, 2% on the next S$180k, 3% on the next S$640k, 4% on the next S$500k, 5% on the next S$1.5M, and 6% above S$3M.

faqs.q: How is Buyer's Stamp Duty calculated in Singapore?
faqs.a: BSD is charged in tiers on the higher of purchase price or market value. Each band of the price is taxed at its own rate, from 1% on the first S$180k up to 6% above S$3M for residential property. On a S$1.5M home the BSD works out to roughly S$44,600. This calculator shows the exact amount in each tier.

faqs.q: Can I use CPF to pay Buyer's Stamp Duty?
faqs.a: For residential property you can generally use CPF to pay BSD, subject to CPF usage rules, though many buyers settle it in cash and reimburse from CPF afterward. For commercial or industrial property, CPF cannot be used and BSD must be paid in cash. Confirm the mechanics with your conveyancer before completion.

faqs.q: When is BSD due and what happens if I pay late?
faqs.a: BSD is payable within 14 days of signing the Option to Purchase exercise or the Sale and Purchase Agreement, whichever is earlier. If the document is executed overseas you get 30 days. Late stamping can trigger a penalty of up to four times the duty, so stamping on time is not optional.

faqs.q: Is BSD different for commercial property?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial or industrial property uses a simpler schedule that tops out at 5% rather than the 6% residential band above S$3M. The lower tiers are the same up to S$1.5M. This calculator lets you toggle between residential and non residential property to see the correct tiered breakdown.

faqs.q: Does the 6% BSD band apply to most buyers?
faqs.a: No. The top 6% rate only applies to the portion of a residential price above S$3M, so most buyers never reach it. On a typical S$1.5M to S$2M purchase your highest band is 5%. Knowing exactly where your bill stacks helps you price shop and budget the cheque intelligently.

tools/foreign-buyer-absd.html.quickAnswer: Since 27 April 2023, foreigners pay 60% ABSD on every Singapore residential purchase, on top of Buyer's Stamp Duty. On a S$2M property that is an extra S$1.2M in ABSD alone, which is why structuring the purchase correctly matters far more than the price you negotiate.

faqs.q: How much ABSD does a foreigner pay to buy property in Singapore?
faqs.a: A foreigner pays 60% ABSD on a residential purchase, applied to the higher of price or market value, on top of tiered BSD. On a S$2M home that is S$1.2M of ABSD before you add the roughly S$69,600 of BSD. This calculator shows your total upfront stamp duty and what it is as a percentage of price.

faqs.q: Are any foreign nationals exempt from the 60% ABSD?
faqs.a: Under certain Free Trade Agreements, nationals of the United States, Switzerland, Norway, Liechtenstein and Iceland are accorded the same stamp duty treatment as Singapore Citizens on residential property. If you hold one of these nationalities you may pay Citizen rates rather than 60%. Verify your eligibility carefully before you rely on it.

faqs.q: Does buying through a company avoid the foreigner ABSD?
faqs.a: No. An entity or company purchasing residential property is charged 65% ABSD, which is higher than the 60% foreigner rate, plus a further non remittable component for developers. A corporate vehicle is generally not a workaround for residential property. It only makes sense in specific commercial scenarios with very different economics.

faqs.q: Should a foreigner wait for PR before buying?
faqs.a: A Singapore PR pays 5% ABSD on a first residential property versus 60% for a foreigner. That 55 percentage point gap is a meaningful reason to time a purchase around obtaining PR if it is realistic for you. The right answer depends on your timeline, so it is worth mapping your specific situation first.

faqs.q: Can a foreigner buy jointly with a Singaporean to lower ABSD?
faqs.a: Where one buyer is a Singapore Citizen and one is a foreigner, IRAS applies the highest rate, 60%, to the whole purchase. Buying jointly does not blend the rate down. Some couples structure ownership around the Citizen spouse, but get this wrong and the full 60% applies, so professional structuring is essential.

absd-calculator.html.quickAnswer: This free calculator applies Singapore's current ABSD rates to your buyer profile, property count and purchase price. Singapore Citizens pay 0%, 20% then 30%; PRs pay 5%, 30% then 35%; foreigners pay a flat 60%; and entities pay 65%, with the higher rate applied on joint purchases.

faqs.q: What ABSD rate applies to a PR buying a first property?
faqs.a: A Singapore PR pays 5% ABSD on a first residential property, then 30% on a second and 35% on a third or more. On a S$1.5M first home that is S$75,000 of ABSD on top of BSD. Select PR and your property count in the calculator to see the exact figure for your price.

faqs.q: How does ABSD work for a joint purchase with mixed profiles?
faqs.a: When buyers have different profiles, such as a Citizen with a PR or foreigner, IRAS charges the highest applicable rate on the entire purchase price rather than splitting it. The calculator reflects this. The practical takeaway is that who is on the title, and in what structure, can change your stamp duty dramatically.

faqs.q: What counts as my property count for ABSD?
faqs.a: Your count includes every residential property you own at the time of purchase, both in Singapore and overseas. A property you part own counts too. So if you already hold one home, your next purchase is usually assessed at the second property rate. Be accurate, because IRAS can reassess and recover any shortfall with penalties.

faqs.q: Is the ABSD figure from this calculator official?
faqs.a: It is an accurate illustration using the current IRAS ABSD schedule and is built for planning, not as a substitute for official assessment. Rates and remission rules can change, so verify the final figure at IRAS.gov.sg and with your conveyancer before transacting. For a full picture across BSD, CPF and loan, book a portfolio analysis.

faqs.q: Can I get ABSD remission or a refund?
faqs.a: Married couples with at least one Singapore Citizen buying their first matrimonial home jointly may apply for ABSD remission. A Citizen couple who buys a second home before selling the first may claim a refund if they sell the original within the required window. Eligibility is conditional, so confirm the exact rules before relying on either.

stamp-duty-calculator.html.quickAnswer: Your total stamp duty in Singapore is BSD plus, where applicable, ABSD. BSD is tiered from 1% to 6% and every buyer pays it. ABSD is layered on top and varies by profile and property count, from 0% for a Citizen first home up to 65% for an entity.

faqs.q: What is the difference between BSD and ABSD?
faqs.a: BSD, Buyer's Stamp Duty, is the base duty every buyer pays, charged in tiers from 1% to 6% of the price. ABSD, Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty, is an extra layer that applies based on your residency and how many homes you own, ranging from 0% to 65%. Your total upfront stamp duty is the two added together.

faqs.q: How much total stamp duty will I pay on a S$1.5M home?
faqs.a: BSD on a S$1.5M residential property is about S$44,600. A Singapore Citizen first time buyer adds 0% ABSD, so the total is roughly S$44,600. A Citizen second property adds 20%, or S$300,000, lifting the total to around S$344,600. Enter your profile and count to see your exact combined figure.

faqs.q: When must stamp duty be paid in Singapore?
faqs.a: BSD and ABSD are both payable within 14 days of signing the Sale and Purchase Agreement or Option to Purchase, or within 30 days if the document is executed overseas. ABSD must be settled in cash. Missing the deadline can attract penalties, so budget the full stamp duty before you commit to the purchase.

faqs.q: Does this calculator handle PR and foreigner buyers?
faqs.a: Yes. You can select Singapore Citizen, PR, foreigner or entity, along with your property count, and the tool applies the correct ABSD rate alongside the tiered BSD. For joint purchases with mixed profiles, remember IRAS applies the highest rate to the whole price, which the rate reference table on the page lays out.

faqs.q: Is stamp duty payable on the price or the valuation?
faqs.a: Both BSD and ABSD are computed on the higher of the purchase price or the market value of the property. If you negotiate a price below valuation, stamp duty is still assessed on the valuation. This matters most on below market or related party transfers, where the duty can exceed what the price alone suggests.

tools/decoupling-calculator.html.quickAnswer: Decoupling is restructuring a jointly owned home so one spouse holds it solo, freeing the other to buy again as a first time owner and avoid the second property ABSD. This calculator weighs the ABSD saved against transfer costs of roughly S$5,000 to S$8,000 and gives an instant verdict on whether it is worth it.

faqs.q: What is property decoupling and how does it work?
faqs.a: Decoupling means transferring one spouse's share of a jointly held property to the other, so only one name remains on it. The exiting spouse then counts as owning no property and can buy a second home at the lower first property ABSD rate. It is a restructuring strategy, not a loophole, and the numbers must justify the costs.

faqs.q: How much does decoupling cost in Singapore?
faqs.a: The main costs are legal fees and BSD on the value of the share being transferred, typically totalling around S$5,000 to S$8,000. There may also be loan restructuring and CPF refund implications. This calculator subtracts those transfer costs from the ABSD you would save to show your net benefit clearly.

faqs.q: When is decoupling worth doing?
faqs.a: As a rule of thumb in this tool, a net benefit above S$15,000 is clearly worth exploring, between S$1 and S$15,000 is marginal and depends on your wider plans, and below zero means transfer costs exceed the ABSD saved. The verdict turns on your property value and ABSD rate, which you enter to get an instant read.

faqs.q: Does decoupling affect my CPF and home loan?
faqs.a: Yes, and these sit outside the headline ABSD maths. The exiting spouse usually has to refund CPF used, with accrued interest, back into their CPF account, and the remaining owner must qualify for the loan on their own income. These factors can change the decision, so they are worth modelling before you proceed.

faqs.q: Is decoupling legal for HDB flats?
faqs.a: HDB stopped allowing part share transfers between owners except in specific circumstances such as divorce, so decoupling is generally a private property strategy rather than an HDB one. This calculator is built for SC, PR and foreigner profiles on private homes. If you hold an HDB flat, the right path is usually different and worth a conversation.
